title: DigitalOcean Managed Agents Brings Managed Cloud Infrastructure to AI Agents
key_facts: DigitalOcean launched DigitalOcean Managed Agents in public preview: a managed cloud layer for AI agents with isolated microVM runtimes, governed tool access and serverless AI inference.
It combines a Harness Runtime and an Action Gateway.

The Harness Runtime gives persistent, isolated compute for agents such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Hermes and LangGraph-built agents; sessions can be paused, resumed or forked, and pause automatically when idle.
The Action Gateway gives agents one MCP endpoint to more than 16,000 tools, including web search, browser automation, DigitalOcean's own APIs and connectors for GitHub, HubSpot and Stripe.
The gateway has central permission settings, requires human approval for sensitive operations, and handles rate limiting, retries and timeouts.

InfoQ says it arrives around the same time as Docker's Cloud Sandboxes; the two overlap, but Docker's is more focused on developer workflows and DigitalOcean's on production infrastructure and orchestration.
Two people quoted on X.com, Elvis Saravia and Ryan Martin, were positive about it.
quote_evidence: DigitalOcean recently launched DigitalOcean Managed Agents in public preview, offering a managed cloud infrastructure layer for AI agents with isolated microVM runtimes, governed tool access, and serverless AI inference.

The gateway implements several security measures, including centralized permission management to define which tools and actions are available to each agent and requiring human approval for sensitive operations.

Docker Cloud Sandboxes are more focused on developer workflows, particularly the ability to move a sandbox between local and cloud compute, while DigitalOcean Managed Agents are more focused on production infrastructure, and provide more orchestration and tool support.
why_it_matters_hint: Another cloud provider is offering ready-made, locked-down places to run AI agents, a task developers have had to build themselves.
event_date: Not stated exactly: InfoQ says "recently launched"; other outlets covered it on 1 to 2 Oct 2026
notes: One outlet (InfoQ) relaying the company announcement; praise quoted is from two people on social media, not tests. It is a public preview. Exact launch date not given in the article, so freshness is NEW with that doubt noted.
